states.description: The state discovery algorithm uses fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis to group UI elements into states. Co-occurrence data is collected via exploration (automated interaction) or recording (manual capture). Each capture produces a fingerprint of visible interactive elements. States are discovered by clustering fingerprints with similar element sets. The algorithm correctness can be verified by examining the discovered states' element lists and confidence scores.

states.description: The state machine follows the multistate model (qontinui/multistate), which extends model-based GUI automation theory. These rules define how states, elements, and screenshots relate to each other. The multistate formal model is Ω = (S, T, G, ω, Td) where S is the set of states, T the transitions, G state groups, ω the occlusion function, and Td dynamic transition generation. All state machine features — discovery, graph editing, state view, screenshots, and export — must conform to these rules. Source: https://qontinui.github.io/multistate/

states.description: Co-occurrence observations drive state element lists via a derive → promote → invalidate → undo loop. The page surface exposes this via ObservationsPanel (mounted below the page header) and ProvenanceBadge (rendered next to each state name in the detail panel). ObservationsPanel shows the most recent drift fit_score (from GET /state-discovery/drift-scores), offers a 'Re-derive all' bulk action (POST /state-discovery/derive?window_days=90), an 'Invalidate spec observations' button (POST /co-occurrence/invalidate — disabled with tooltip when the StateMachineConfig has no spec_id), and an invalidation log table fed by GET /co-occurrence/invalidations. Each invalidation is grouped by undo_token; rows within the 24 h window show an Undo button (POST /co-occurrence/invalidate/undo). ProvenanceBadge renders three variants — green 'observed' (with support/contrast tooltip + observation count + age), gray 'ai-generated', yellow 'ai-fallback' (with invalidation age). Missing provenance on older compiled SMs silently falls back to 'ai-generated'.
states.precondition: No invalidations have been emitted for this spec within the current window

description: UI Bridge State Machine page — connect to SDK-integrated apps, discover UI states via automated exploration or manual recording with fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis, then manage state machine configs across seven tabs: Discovery (SDK app connection, explore/record data collection, fingerprint-based state discovery with auto-save), Graph Editor (interactive dagre node-edge layout with element thumbnails, drag-and-drop element reassignment, transition creation), State View (list + spatial + screenshot modes via shared StateViewPanel), Transitions (list with action playback via shared TransitionsPanel), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states via shared PathfindingPanel), Exploration Results (dashboard with pass rate, coverage stats, discrepancy severity groups, history list, and per-state detail with confidence scores, element verification, and AI analysis prompt), and Export (save to JSON file or load into Python runtime).
